title: OIDC RP-Initiated Logout
subtitle: The app kills its own session, then redirects to the IdP’s end_session_endpoint with an id_token_hint — a fully browser-visible chain of redirects.

steps.label: User clicks “Log out”
steps.lede: The user starts logout in the app (the RP). What follows is a short chain of redirects: RP → IdP → back to RP.
steps.devtools: Open DevTools (F12) → Network, enable Preserve log — without it the early hops vanish as the browser navigates. This whole flow is browser-visible.

steps.label: RP local logout
steps.lede: The RP destroys its own session first — clearing its cookie before handing off — so logout holds even if the user never finishes the IdP leg. It then redirects to end_session.

headers: rp1_session=; Path=/; Max-Age=0; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax

steps.devtools: Filter on logout. Confirm the Set-Cookie actually clears rp1_session (Max-Age=0) — the RP kills its session before the redirect. Read the Location header: it points at the IdP end_session_endpoint and carries id_token_hint, post_logout_redirect_uri, and state.

steps.label: GET /end_session at the IdP
steps.lede: The browser hits end_session with the IdP session cookie attached. The id_token_hint identifies which session to end and lets the IdP skip the “Are you sure?” prompt.

headers: idp_session=; Path=/; Max-Age=0; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=None

jwt.title: Decoded id_token_hint
payload: This RP’s client_id — the IdP validates aud
May be EXPIRED and still accepted as a hint
Session id — the exact SSO session to terminate

steps.devtools: Filter on end_session. Decode the id_token_hint for sub/sid. The IdP validates the hint’s signature and aud, not its exp — an expired hint still identifies the session fine. Confirm the response clears idp_session and that post_logout_redirect_uri exactly matches one registered for the client.

steps.label: Terminate SSO session
steps.lede: The IdP validates the hint, matches it to the current session, verifies the redirect URI is registered (exact match), and terminates the SSO session — clearing its own cookie.
steps.devtools: Not a separate network row. If this deployment chains into front-channel logout you’ll ALSO see hidden frontchannel-logout iframe requests on the IdP page; if it chains into back-channel logout, those logout_token POSTs are server-to-server and will not appear in DevTools.

steps.label: Post-logout redirect back to the RP
steps.lede: The IdP 302s the browser to the registered post_logout_redirect_uri, echoing state. The RP shows its “logged out” page after confirming state matches.
steps.devtools: Filter on loggedout. Read the state query param — the RP compares it to what it stored. If the URI had not been registered, this hop would not happen: you’d land on the IdP’s own logged-out page instead. An unregistered post_logout_redirect_uri must never become an open redirect.

steps.label: “You have been logged out”
steps.lede: Sign-out is complete at both the RP and the IdP. Because the RP cleared its session in step one, the logout held regardless of how the IdP leg resolved.
steps.devtools: Alternate to recognize: with no id_token_hint, the end_session response is a 200 HTML “Do you want to log out?” prompt rather than a 302 — you’ll see the GET return a document, then a POST when the user confirms.
